thresholds.title: Thresholds
thresholds.help: Empty = no limit. A value above "Down above" or below "Down below" sets the channel to Down; otherwise the warning limits apply.

channels.title: Notification channels
channels.recipientsHint: 1–20 addresses, one per line or comma-separated. The SMTP server is set in Settings.
channels.testSavedHint: Sends a test with the saved settings — save first.

rules.title: Alert rules
rules.onStatusesHint: "Up" only fires on recovery from Down or Warning.
rules.delayHint: Send only if the status still holds after this delay.

settings.title: Settings
settings.retentionHint: History older than this is deleted.
settings.defaultIntervalHint: Used for new sensors without an interval.
settings.defaultLanguageHint: For the login page and notifications.
settings.publicBaseUrlHint: Used for links in notifications. Empty = no links.
settings.smtpTestHint: Uses the saved settings — save first.
settings.timezoneHint: Used for weekly maintenance windows and the times in notifications.
settings.topologyRefreshHint: How often LLDP/CDP neighbours are read. 0 = off.

ports.title: Ports
ports.intro: Port inventory reads each switch's interfaces, VLANs, MAC table and PoE, and ARP from routers.
ports.thresholdHint: A port with more MACs than this is treated as an uplink (1–1000).
ports.retentionHint: How long MACs and IPs that disappeared are kept (1–365).
ports.reverseDnsHint: Look up host names (PTR) of the IPs learned from ARP.

users.title: Users
users.passwordKeepHint: Leave empty to keep the current password.

account.title: My account
account.languageHint: Your interface language is saved automatically when you change it in the top bar.

snmp_interface.speed_bps_override: Empty = the speed reported by the device

http.url: {host} is replaced with the device host
http.keyword: Optional text to look for in the response

dns.server: Empty = use the device host as the DNS server
dns.expected: Optional; at least one answer must equal it

snmp_custom.oid: Numeric dotted OID, e.g. 1.3.6.1.2.1.1.3.0 (MIB names are not accepted)
snmp_custom.unit: Shown next to the value, e.g. °C, clients, pages (max 16 characters)
snmp_custom.multiplier: Applied to the raw value (gauge) or the rate (counter), e.g. 8 for octets → bit/s, 0.1 for tenths
snmp_custom.label: Optional; shown in the status message
snmp_custom.percent_of_oid: Optional; value = raw ÷ this OID × 100 (the multiplier is ignored)
snmp_custom.expected: Empty = any text is OK; otherwise the value must match
snmp_custom.percent_base: Total: value ÷ divisor OID. Sum: value ÷ (value + other OID), e.g. used next to free.

snmp_disk.storage_descr: Exactly as reported by the device, e.g. / or C:\

snmp_walk_count.count_values: Comma-separated integers; empty = every row matches.

storage.title: Storage reported by the device
storage.manualHint: Or enter the storage description below.

telegram.helpTitle: How do I get a bot token and chat ID?
telegram.help1: In Telegram, open <c>@BotFather</c>, send <c>/newbot</c> and follow the steps. BotFather replies with the bot token (e.g. <c>123456789:AAE…</c>). Keep it secret.
telegram.help2: Private chat: open your bot and press Start. Group: add the bot to the group and send a message there. Channel: add the bot as an administrator.
telegram.help3: Then open the following address in a browser and copy the number after <c>"id"</c> in the <c>"chat"</c> section:
telegram.help4: Group and channel IDs are negative (supergroups start with <c>-100</c>). For a public channel you can also use <c>@channelname</c>.
telegram.botTokenHint: From <c>@BotFather</c>. Write-only: it is never shown again.
telegram.tokenInvalid: Expected digits, a colon and the key, e.g. 123456789:AAE…
telegram.chatIdHint: <c>-100…</c> for groups/channels, a number for a private chat, or <c>@channelname</c>

templates.title: Device templates
templates.subtitle: Built-in sets of sensors. Applying a template adds only what is missing.
templates.applyHint: Sensors that already exist are skipped. Entries marked “if available” are checked on the device first.
templates.applying: Checking the device… this can take up to two minutes.
templates.unverifiedHint: Not yet tested on real equipment; OIDs may need corrections.
templates.loadErrors_one: {{count}} template file could not be loaded
templates.loadErrors_other: {{count}} template files could not be loaded
templates.libraryLine: {{builtin}} built-in and {{user}} user templates, {{errors}} load errors
templates.userDirHint: Copy a built-in template file into this folder, edit it and press “Reload templates”. Keep the same id to replace a built-in, or use a new id.
templates.confidenceTitle: Confidence in the OIDs of this entry

discovery.title: Discovery
discovery.subtitle: Scan address ranges, recognise devices and add them with a template.
discovery.targetsHint: One per line: CIDR (<c>192.168.1.0/24</c>), range (<c>192.168.1.10-50</c> or <c>10.0.0.1-10.0.1.20</c>), IPv4/IPv6 address or hostname. Up to 64 entries and 4096 hosts.

targetError.invalid: not an address, range, CIDR or hostname
targetError.order: the range ends before it starts

discovery.targetGroupHint: Its SNMP credentials are tried first; imported devices go here by default.
discovery.extraCredsHint: Tried after the target group's credentials. Write-only: never shown again after saving.

err.probes: Enable at least one of Ping, SNMP or TCP.
err.communities: Up to 5 communities of at most 64 characters.
err.v3: Up to 3 v3 users, each with a username.

discovery.scopeNote: Only the listed addresses are probed (ping, TCP connect, SNMP read, reverse DNS).
discovery.deleteRunningHint: A running scan cannot be deleted.
discovery.scheduleHint: Off by default. The first scheduled run only records a baseline.
discovery.notifyHint: Without channels only an event is written.
discovery.deleteProfileConfirm: Delete profile "{{name}}"? Its past scans are kept.
discovery.polling: Live updates unavailable — refreshing every 2 s
discovery.cancelConfirm: Stop the scan now? Hosts found so far are kept.
discovery.waitingResults: Scanning… found hosts appear here as they answer.
discovery.importAfterScan: Import is available when the scan has finished.
discovery.importMaybePartial: The import may have partly completed. The list was refreshed: hosts that were imported now show as Imported; the rest are still selected, so you can retry just those.
discovery.importBudget: the import ran out of time before this host
discovery.retrySelected: Hosts to retry are still selected.
discovery.profileSavedBusy: Profile "{{name}}" saved; a scan is already running — run it later.
discovery.fingerprintHint: Reads the web page title, server header and SSH/telnet banner of hosts with ports 80/443/8080/8443/22/23 open, to recognise devices without SNMP. Sends no credentials.

ack.commentHint: Optional, e.g. "Replacing PSU, ETA 14:00". Shown to everyone.
ack.explain: Acknowledging silences further problem, escalation and reminder notifications for this problem. The status is unchanged, and the acknowledgement clears automatically on the next status change. Recovery is still notified.
ack.title: Acknowledge {{name}}

dependency.title: Dependency
dependency.deviceHint: When the parent device is down, sensors of this device that fail are shown as unreachable and do not alert.
dependency.groupHint: Devices of this group (and subgroups) that inherit use this parent. A device that is itself the parent is not affected.
dependency.sensorHint: The parent counts as down when this sensor is down. Automatic = its ping sensor, else all its sensors.
dependency.parentDownSuffix: is down — sensors that fail are shown as unreachable.

maintenance.title: Maintenance windows
maintenance.globalBanner: Maintenance "{{name}}" is active for all devices until {{time}}. Notifications are paused.
maintenance.tzNote: Times are in the server time zone:
maintenance.noOccurrences: No occurrence in the next 14 days.

empty.active: No window is active right now.

err.endBeforeStart: The end must be after the start.

escalation.title: Escalation and reminders
escalation.help: Escalation sends the problem to more channels when it is neither acknowledged nor recovered after the given time (measured from when the problem began). Reminders repeat the notification to the rule channels. Both stop when the problem is acknowledged, recovers, or the device is in maintenance.
escalation.afterHint: From the start of the problem; at least the delay above (1 minute to 7 days).
escalation.channelsHint: Who gets the escalation (e.g. the on-call manager). The recovery is sent to them too.
escalation.repeatHint: Sent to the rule channels; 5 minutes to 7 days.

err.afterDelay: Must be at least the delay.
err.channels: Choose at least one escalation channel.
err.statuses: Escalation and reminders need Down or Warning in the statuses.

identify.title: Identity
identify.running: Identifying the device (SNMP, ports, web/SSH fingerprint)… up to 40 seconds.

valueMap.hint: Integer value → status and text. Values not listed use the default status.

err.duplicate: Each value may appear only once.

topology.title: Network map
topology.resetConfirm: Forget all node positions and arrange the map automatically again?
topology.deleteStaleConfirm_one: Delete {{count}} stale link? Links reported again are re-created by the next refresh.
topology.deleteStaleConfirm_other: Delete {{count}} stale links? Links reported again are re-created by the next refresh.
topology.empty: No devices to show. Add devices with SNMP sensors and refresh the topology.
topology.hint: Click a device to open it, a link or an unmanaged neighbour for details. Drag to arrange; pinch or scroll to zoom.
topology.unmanagedHint: Reported by LLDP/CDP but not monitored.
topology.deleteDiscoveredHint: A discovered link comes back with the next refresh if the switches still report it.
topology.noInterfaces: Interfaces could not be read; type the port name.
topology.suggestHint: Parents derived from the links (walking out from the root). Review and apply the ones you want; nothing is changed automatically.
topology.rootHint: Usually the core switch or router. Empty = the device with the most links.
topology.noSuggestions: No suggestions: there are no links from the root.

find.title: Find MAC / IP
find.subtitle: Where is a device connected? Searches the MAC tables of every switch.

find.help: The MAC tables are read with the port inventory of each switch; IP addresses come from routers and firewalls with “Collect ARP”.

device.inventoryHint: Auto: ports for switches, ARP for routers/firewalls (needs an SNMP sensor).
